llm.summary: The skill appears to do hotel search as advertised, but it under-discloses its proxy backend and ships a live proxy token in source code.

dimensions.detail: The script is coherent with the stated purpose: it searches Courtyard/Marriott hotels, fetches details and packages, and returns booking links without directly booking or modifying accounts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The README says data comes from multi-platform direct connections, while the code sends all requests to a single Tencent SCF fliggy-proxy endpoint; the data flow is partially disclosed but the real backend and trust boundary are not clearly named.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package is a simple skill with one Python script and no install-time execution, but metadata marks apiKeyRequired as false even though the script contains and uses a proxy token.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime behavior is limited to user-directed hotel queries over a fixed HTTPS endpoint and does not read local files, spawn background workers, or request broad system access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The script hard-codes a live X-Proxy-Token and sends it on every request, creating credential exposure and an unclear shared-authentication model for the proxy service.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this before installing. It should only send hotel-search parameters to a fixed external proxy and return links, but the proxy provider and token model are not well disclosed. Avoid using it for sensitive travel details unless you are comfortable with those queries going through the publisher's proxy service.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Network transfer of city, date, hotel name, and keyword parameters is expected for real-time hotel search, and SKILL.md does disclose a proxy data flow, but it does not fully declare or identify the external endpoint in metadata.
[TP4] unexpected: The artifact supports the mismatch concern: SKILL.md claims multi-platform direct data access, while the code uses one fliggy-proxy SCF backend with token authentication.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The hard-coded proxy token is present in source and is not necessary to expose to users as distributed skill code, even though authenticated proxy access may be needed for the feature.
